    feat(scan): report what a COPY of the whole build context takes into the image (§3.81)
    
    A `COPY . .` sends every file no .dockerignore leaves out into a layer of
    the image. Neither trivy config nor hadolint has a rule for it, and the
    secret stages cannot see it: they read the working tree, and .git matches no
    secret pattern although its history keeps every secret ever committed.
    
    DevDesk now checks it itself, in a build-context stage that runs with the
    Misconfiguration category and needs no tool. A finding requires three facts,
    all verified: a COPY/ADD of the whole context in the final stage or a stage
    it is built FROM; a .git directory or a sensitive file (.env, *.pem, *.key,
    id_rsa, credentials.json, .npmrc) on disk; and no ignore file that may apply
    (the context's .dockerignore, or BuildKit's <Dockerfile>.dockerignore)
    excluding it. The .dockerignore reader follows Docker's syntax and attaches
    a certainty to every answer; anything uncertain is silence. Only root
    Dockerfiles are checked, since a deeper one does not say where its context is.
    
    DEVDESK-CTX-001 (.git) is fixed by ctrl+o, which appends .git to the one
    existing ignore file; it declines with none (DevDesk does not create one) or
    two. The fix edits a file other than the finding's, so remediation.Rule
    gains a Target and the security view keeps the finding's file apart from the
    written one for the verification re-scan. DEVDESK-CTX-002 has no fix.
    
    IsDockerfileName no longer mistakes Dockerfile.dockerignore for a Dockerfile.

--- 5c0d1459 feat(scan): re-scan a floating base image instead of trusting its cached count (§3.79) ---
A base image on a tag with no version (latest, an untagged reference, main,
a codename, a dhi.io tag rebuilt in place) had no candidates and said so in a
reason shared with digest-pinned references. Its cached count was kept for 24
hours, keyed by a reference that never changes when the registry replaces
what it points to.

- remediation.Ref.Floats: no digest and no version in the tag.
- Entry.Floating, with its own reason (ReasonFloating); a digest-only
  reference now says it is pinned (ReasonPinnedByDigest).
- The Remediation tab's S re-scans a floating image every time, whatever the
  age of its cached result. Nothing is written: pinning by digest would stop
  the image following upstream fixes, and stays a separate feature.

A versioned tag republished in place is not detected; that would need the
registry's current digest for the tag. Documented as still open.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: ac3fe2b2da75

--- 71c45596 feat(images): an Update column that says when a registry holds a newer image (§3.88) ---
Images, containers and the Remediation tab now show an arrow when an image's
registry holds something newer: a later patch tag on the same line
(20.11.1 -> 20.11.4, same variant), or new content behind the same tag
("new build"), which is the only update a floating tag ever gets.

- internal/imageupdate: Check asks each registry (at most four at once) and
  caches the tag's digest and newer patch in image-updates.json, 6 hours,
  30 minutes for a failure. Evaluate compares with the local digests when a
  row is built, so a pull clears the arrow without asking again. Tracker is
  what a view keeps between checks.
- oci.ManifestDigest: a HEAD on the manifest accepting an OCI index and a
  Docker manifest list, so a multi-platform tag's digest matches the one
  `docker pull` records. RegistryAPIBase moves from the Remediation tab to oci.
- docker: Image.RepoDigests from the existing image inspect call;
  ContainerImageDigests compares a container through the image it was created
  from, so a pull does not clear its arrow until it is recreated;
  ImageRepoDigests for Dockerfile bases.
- internal/ui/updatecol: one column definition for the three tables, coloured
  with a new ColorUpdateAvailable alias. Only pulled images are asked about;
  a locally built image has no digest to compare.

The containers table is the widest: its two gauges, dropped first (§3.71),
now need 180 columns instead of 160.

--- 7f6df226 fix(images): keep "new build" whole in the Update column (§3.88) ---
The column follows its content, and a content column shrinks to its MinWidth
before any column is dropped. Floored at the title's six cells, the label
rendered as "new…" in oci's Images tab. The floor is now the width of the
arrow and "new build", the one label known in advance; a longer patch tag may

Entire-Checkpoint: e4d5489ed695

--- c4fd1d33 feat(images): say why the Update column shows no arrow (§3.88) ---
A blank cell stood for up to date, not comparable and failed alike. In the
Remediation tab, where bases are rarely pinned and often not held by the
engine, the column was silent without saying why.

Every state now has its own grey text: a check mark (up to date), "checking"
(no answer yet), "?" (the registry did not answer), "local build" (no registry
digest), "not local" (a Dockerfile base the engine does not hold), "pinned"
(a digest with no tag). Blank is left for what the question does not apply
to. Evaluate takes what an empty local digest list means to its caller.

The column's filter only matches an update's label, or a search for "ca"
would find every "local build".

Entire-Checkpoint: 3759e98efef8

--- f590d72f feat(images): G updates an image and removes the one it replaces (§3.88) ---
On the Images tab, G pulls what the Update column points at (the newer patch
tag, or the same tag for a new build), then removes the replaced image by ID,
never forced.

It refuses while any container, running or stopped, was created from that
image. The check runs twice: from the engine's container count to grey G with
its reason (Rule 130; docker only), and against the engine just before the
pull (`ps -a --filter ancestor=`), which covers a container created in between
and podman. The footer names the containers in use. A pull that brings the
image already held removes nothing, and a removal the engine refuses leaves the
old image with a warning.

It runs as a pull job, so the row spins and K stops it.

Pas vraiment à cause de la taille en soi — git gère un fichier de 15 000 lignes sans problème, et `CLAUDE.md` ne l'importe pas via `@`, donc il ne charge pas le contexte de chaque session automatiquement. Le vrai coût est déjà documenté dans `.claude/CLAUDE.md` : chaque branche insère son entrée en tête de section (§1.1, ou le prochain numéro §3.x), donc fusionner plusieurs branches parties du même commit produit systématiquement un conflit au même endroit — vécu à chaque squash-merge fait aujourd'hui. Plus le fichier grossit, plus il y a de branches concurrentes candidates à ce même point d'insertion, donc cette friction augmente avec le volume, même si chaque conflit individuel reste trivial à résoudre (garder les deux côtés).

L'archivage du **done** réduit un peu la marge de collision en éloignant les entrées fermées du point d'insertion actif, mais ça ne supprime pas le mécanisme — tant que toutes les branches ajoutent en tête de la même sous-section, le risque de conflit reste proportionnel au nombre de branches en vol, pas à la taille totale du fichier.
